text:
Dear YOSHIKI, 
I am a fan of X JAPAN from Taiwan. 
I first started listening to X JAPAN when I was in high school, around 1996. 
At that time, hearing X JAPAN for the first time was truly shocking in the best possible way. Your music felt incredibly ahead of its time. The melodies, arrangements, stage presence, and visual style were unlike anything I had ever experienced before. 
From that moment on, I became deeply attached to X JAPAN. 
I love X JAPAN, and I love every member of the band. 
But if I had to choose, the two people I have always felt especially close to are you, YOSHIKI, and HIDE. 
I have watched this video many, many times. 
And for some reason, every time I watch it, I feel a deep sadness in my heart. 
Maybe it is because, through your expressions, your eyes, and some of the things you have said over the years, I feel that you have carried a great deal of sorrow inside you for a very long time. 
Because of that, I also started looking back at many of the things you have said publicly in the past. 
And the more I read, the more I wanted to tell you something. 
YOSHIKI, please do not keep blaming yourself. 
Your very existence has already comforted, supported, and even healed so many people around the world. 
Including me. 
I have always felt that you are a very kind-hearted person, and someone who cares deeply about the people around you. 
You love your family. You treasure your friends. You have always kept HIDE close to your heart. 
And I think that fans who have loved X JAPAN for many years can feel how much every member of the band means to you. 
Some people are gone. 
Some things can never return to the way they once were. 
But you have never forgotten them. 
That alone is deeply moving. 
So I truly hope you will not carry every regret, every sadness, or every sense of responsibility on your own shoulders. 
You have already done so much. 
And I believe you have given far more to this world than you may realize. 
There was only one small thing that made me a little sad while watching the video. 
It is really just a tiny thing, so please do not take it too seriously. 
As a fan from Taiwan, when I saw people from around the world singing "ENDLESS RAIN," part of me hoped I would also see Taiwanese fans in the video. 
But I do not think I saw anyone from Taiwan. 
For a moment, I did feel a little disappointed. 
But it is really okay. 
Because I know your love reaches fans all over the world. 
Nationality is not what matters most. 
And whether Taiwan appeared in that video or not, we have always been here. 
There have always been many people in Taiwan who love X JAPAN, and many people here who continue to love your music. 
I am one of them. 
It has been so many years since 1996. 
A lot has changed, and I am no longer the high school student I once was. 
But whenever I hear X JAPAN again, so many of those feelings still come back. 
So there is something I want to say to you. 
Thank you for still being here. 
Thank you for never giving up on music. 
Thank you for leaving us so many songs and so much music that have stayed with us through different stages of our lives. 
I will always love X JAPAN. 
And I will always support you. 
And one last thing, just to make it clear— 
I am a man, and I am straight. :) 
But I really do love you, YOSHIKI. 
Please take good care of yourself. 
With love and respect from Taiwan, 
A longtime X JAPAN fan since 1996♥

Everyone will one day drift away from us,
just like raindrops falling from the sky—
appearing for a moment, touching the earth,
and then slowly fading into nothingness.

And no one is exempt from this truth.
Not even ourselves.

Life is fleeting.
Like a raindrop, we arrive in this world,
remain for but a brief moment,
and eventually return to where we came from.

So while the rain is falling,
do not merely watch it pass.

Feel the raindrops upon your skin.
Listen to the gentle sound of the rain.
Feel the coolness and freshness carried by each drop.

For one day, even these moments will pass.

The rain teaches us something simple:
everything that arises must eventually cease.
Nothing remains forever, and nothing can be held onto forever.

Yet while we are still here,
while we can still hear, feel, breathe, and be touched by the world,
let us truly be present.

For the rain is not merely falling from the sky.

It is quietly reminding us
that we are still alive.
